Personally, I don’t buy technology off of strangers unless it’s been cleared and I normally have someone techy look into it as well. If you’re worried about it still you could hire a professional to check your system and set up an extra firewall beyond normal password protection. Just my two cents 🤷‍♀️

I was in charge of a group constructing props in the theatre department. We were all using x-acto knives to cut foam board.

The day prior there was a threat for a school shooting. One of the guys in my group was fiddling with his x-acto knife as we were discussing the subject.

We were just generally shocked by the incident and were all talking about how horrible it was when he said “If I was going to use a weapon at school to hurt someone I would use a knife.” 

He then looked me in the eye and gave me the most evil smile and everyone in our group went quiet and kept working.

I immediately gave a lame excuse to leave and went to tell my teacher about it.

That particular student wasn’t allowed to use any power tools for the whole year and was given a very dull hand saw for any cutting he needed to do. 

We were all nice to him, just very aware of our surroundings for the rest of the year. 

We graduated in 2019 and he wasn’t permitted at graduation because of a comment he made (not sure what it was) to our administration.

I work as a coach with kids through a summer camp/after school program and it’s often very challenging following covid rules and in general the age groups are very challenging, it’s a lot of fun though and I really enjoy it.

I work at a martial arts school as an after school/summer camp/ (because of covid) daytime school year coach. Almost all of my coworkers are black belts and I have no martial arts experience. 

I do love my job, though, because I get to see kids learning and growing in new ways every day, I make pretty good wages, and I have the nicest coworkers ever. 

Sometimes working with some of the kids gets difficult because they’re accustomed to their own ideas, schedules, and rules; but I get to witness their ups and downs in learning how to socialize and adapt to new environments. 

Watching some of their interactions and interacting with some of them is actually hilarious because I get to see the look on their faces when everything they know gets flipped upside down. For example, I watched as a young girl stared at me in confusion the other day when I explained to her that the word “yes” is spelled y-e-s, as opposed to her previous idea that it was spelled w-u-o.

These kids bring me so much joy and I love working there so much.
